title: The dual localization boundary transposes to evaluation followed by the support boundary
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use ordinary small-etale derived categories of modules over the constant sheaves $A$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], and inverse/direct images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Use the support right adjoint $Ri^!$ and the support triangle [lem-exc-closed-ambient, lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. Put $E=Ri^!A_X$ and $B=i^*Rj_*A_U$. Let $b:B\to E[1]$ be the restriction by $i^*$ of the boundary of $i_*E\to A_X\to Rj_*A_U\to i_*E[1]$, using $i^*i_*E=E$.

Let $L$ be a finite locally free $A_U$-module sheaf (etale locally $A_U^r$ for a finite integer $r$), put $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_A(L,A_U)$, and suppose $K=Rj_*L$ has bounded cohomology. Set $C=i^*Rj_*L$ and $C'=i^*Rj_*L^\vee$. Apply [lem-per-etale-internal-hom-localization] to $(K,A_X)$ and rotate to obtain
$$R\mathcal Hom_A(K,A_X)\longrightarrow Rj_*L^\vee\xrightarrow{u}i_*R\mathcal Hom_A(C,E)[1]\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(K,A_X)[1].$$
Then the tensor--Hom transpose on $Z$ of $i^*u:C'\to R\mathcal Hom_A(C,E)[1]$ is, up to an overall sign $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ determined only by the shift and rotation conventions, the composite
$$C'\otimes_A^LC\xrightarrow{\mathrm{cup}}i^*Rj_*(L^\vee\otimes_A^LL)\xrightarrow{i^*Rj_*(\mathrm{ev})}B\xrightarrow{b}E[1].$$
Here cup is the canonical direct-image tensor map, the mate under $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ of the tensor of the two counits, and $\mathrm{ev}(f\otimes x)=f(x)$. The transpose uses the evaluation normalization of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. The comparison is natural in $L$. It asserts an identity of the specified maps; it asserts neither perfectness of the pairing nor biduality nor constructibility.

source.place: Tag 08JC, lemma-RHom-triangulated, together with the evaluation construction in section internal-hom: formal boundary-mate comparison for the open/closed internal-Hom triangle. The comparison is agent-supplied from these constructions, not a verbatim Stacks theorem.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat complex $P$ with flat terms representing $K$, and a bounded-below injective resolution $A_X\to I$. Constant-coefficient inverse images are exact, and $i^*P,j^*P$ are K-flat with flat terms. Set $T=i^!_0I$, $S=i_*T$, and $J=j_*j^*I$, where $i^!_0F=i^*\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$. The closed support adjunction makes each $T^q$ injective. Exactness of $i^*$ and its adjunction with $i_*$ make each $S^q$ injective. Similarly $j^*I^q$ is injective because $j^*$ is right adjoint to exact $j_!$, and $J^q$ is injective because $j_*$ is right adjoint to exact $j^*$. Thus $I,T,S,J$ are bounded below and K-injective. The right-derived computation gives $J\simeq Rj_*A_U$, and $T$ computes the right derived functor of $i^!_0$ at $A_X$ used in the internal-Hom localization lemma. It is also the value at $A_X$ of the support right adjoint of the statement, with matching counit: for every complex $G$ on $Z$, naturally in $G$, $\operatorname{Hom}_D(i_*G,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(i_*G,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(G,T)=\operatorname{Hom}_D(G,T)$, by the K-injective Hom lemma for $I$ and for $T$ and the termwise adjunction $i_*\dashv i^!_0$ on homotopy categories. So $T$ with the support inclusion $i_*T\to I$ represents $\operatorname{Hom}_D(i_*-,A_X)$, and Yoneda gives $T\simeq E$ carrying this inclusion to the counit of $i_*\dashv Ri^!$. These choices require neither finite Tor dimension of $K$ nor boundedness of $Rj_*L^\vee$.

source.place: 08JC setup; 09XQ (etale-cohomology-lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic); K-flat and injective models of section-internal-hom

proof.text: For each etale $V\to X$, the map $I^q(V)\to I^q(V\times_XU)$ is surjective: $V\times_XU\to V$ is a monomorphism in the small etale site, so apply the ringed-site injective restriction lemma. The inverse-image/restriction identification says that this is exactly the component of $I^q\to j_*j^*I^q$. Its kernel $F^q$ restricts to zero on $U$, since restriction of the open unit to $U$ is the identity. The open/closed exact sequence applied to $F^q$ therefore identifies $F^q\to i_*i^*F^q$ with an isomorphism. This identifies the kernel inclusion with $S^q\to I^q$, naturally and $A$-linearly. We obtain a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to S\xrightarrow{a}I\to J\to0$. Each degree splits because $S^q$ is injective (extend $1_{S^q}$ across $S^q\hookrightarrow I^q$); no splitting is claimed to be a chain map. Its cone-to-quotient roof $d:J\leftarrow\operatorname{Cone}(a)\to S[1]$, with the sign $-p$ of the cone triangle, makes $S\to I\to J\xrightarrow{d}S[1]$ distinguished. The cited support triangle fixes only its first two arrows, but its boundary is still determined: $J$ is K-injective, so $\operatorname{Hom}_D(S[1],J)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(S[1],j_*j^*I)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(j^*S[1],j^*I)=0$, as $j^*S=j^*i_*T=0$ ($(i_*T)(V\times_XU)=T(\emptyset)=0$). By part (2) of the triangle-morphism lemma, the identity of $A_X\simeq I$ with $i_*E\simeq S$ (Step 1) and $Rj_*A_U\simeq J$ is a morphism from the support triangle to this one, so its boundary corresponds to $d$.

Write $H_S=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,S)$, $H=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$, and $Q=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,J)$. Applying Hom to the degreewise splittings of Step 2 gives a degreewise split exact sequence $0\to H_S\xrightarrow{a_H}H\to Q\to0$: a degree-$n$ lift is the product of the lifts into $I^{p+n}$, for all $p$. Products are sectionwise, so this is a splitting of module sheaves in each degree, even when $P$ is unbounded. Its boundary is the roof $\delta:Q\leftarrow\operatorname{Cone}(a_H)\to H_S[1]$, with the same sign $-p$ as $d$, so $H_S\to H\to Q\xrightarrow{\delta}H_S[1]$ is distinguished. The Hom differential is $d(f)=d_I f-(-1)^{|f|}f d_P$. Hence these complexes compute the derived Homs into $S,I,J$, respectively; in particular $H$ represents $R\mathcal Hom(K,A_X)$.

Compare this exact sequence with the Hom of $0\to j_!j^*P\to P\to i_*i^*P\to0$. On each etale slice, open adjunction and inverse-image/direct-image adjunction give
$\mathcal Hom(j_!j^*P^p,I^q)=j_*\mathcal Hom(j^*P^p,j^*I^q)=\mathcal Hom(P^p,j_*j^*I^q)$.
Both maps from $\mathcal Hom(P^p,I^q)$ are restriction of a map to the open. Their common kernel consists precisely of maps factoring through $P^p\to i_*i^*P^p$, and also of maps with image in $S^q=\ker(I^q\to J^q)$. This gives $\mathcal Hom(i_*i^*P^p,I^q)=\mathcal Hom(P^p,S^q)$, compatibly with the inclusions into $\mathcal Hom(P^p,I^q)$. Taking products over $p$ gives an isomorphism of short exact sequences of Hom complexes, with middle map the identity; naturality of these adjunctions commutes with the displayed Hom differential. Thus their cone roofs agree, including their last maps, up to the fixed contravariant-Hom rotation sign. This compares the actual connecting maps, not merely the first two arrows of abstract distinguished triangles.

source.place: 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), termwise split Hom argument, expanded on the open/closed sequence; section-internal-hom

proof.text: The closed sheaf internal adjunction identifies $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(i_*i^*P,I)$ with $i_*\mathcal Hom^\bullet(i^*P,T)$: $i_*$ preserves the products by its section formula, and the adjunction commutes with the differential. Therefore $H_S$ represents $i_*R\mathcal Hom(C,E)$. On the open, $j^*P$ is K-flat and $j^*I$ K-injective, so $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(j^*P,j^*I)$ is K-injective and its $j_*$ computes its derived direct image. Here $j^*P\simeq j^*Rj_*L\simeq L$, since $j^*j_*F=F$ termwise for an injective resolution $F$ of $L$ (inverse image along $j$ is restriction to $U$, and $(j_*F)(V)=F(V\times_XU)=F(V)$ for $V$ over $U$). Locally where $L=A_U^r$, finite direct-sum Hom identifies $R\mathcal Hom(L,A_U)$ with $L^\vee$ in degree zero; this identification glues since it sends a functional to that same functional. Thus $Q$ represents $Rj_*L^\vee$. By Step 4 these identifications carry the first two arrows of the internal-Hom localization triangle to $H_S\to H\to Q$. Its third arrow is then determined: $Q\cong j_*\mathcal Hom^\bullet(j^*P,j^*I)$ is K-injective and $j^*H_S=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(j^*P,j^*S)=0$, so $\operatorname{Hom}_D(H_S[1],Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(j^*H_S[1],\mathcal Hom^\bullet(j^*P,j^*I))=0$. Part (2) of the triangle-morphism lemma makes these identifications a morphism of triangles, so the boundary $u$ of the question is $\epsilon\delta$, with $\epsilon$ depending only on the cone/rotation conventions.

source.place: 08JC and section-internal-hom; 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective); closed endpoint of ILO XVII 7.6.10

proof.text:
For $M=S,I,J$ use the chain evaluation $e_M:\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,M)\otimes P\to M$, $f\otimes x\mapsto f(x)$. It is a chain map: for $|f|=n$ the two terms $-(-1)^nf(d_Px)$ from $d(f)(x)$ and $(-1)^nf(d_Px)$ from the tensor differential cancel, leaving $d_M(f(x))$. The evaluations commute with $a$ and $I\to J$. They extend to a map $\operatorname{Cone}(a_H)\otimes P\to\operatorname{Cone}(a)$ by $(h,s)\otimes x\mapsto(h(x),s(x))$. With $\operatorname{Cone}(a_H)^n=H^n\oplus H_S^{n+1}$, the second component has differential $-d(s)$; its tensor differential is $-d(s)\otimes1+(-1)^n s\otimes d_P$, which evaluates to $-d_S(s(x))$. This verifies the cone map including the shifted summand. It commutes with both cone projections and both cone-to-quotient maps. Since $P$ is K-flat, tensoring the quasi-isomorphism $\operatorname{Cone}(a_H)\to Q$ with $P$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The two roofs therefore give the equality of derived morphisms
$$e_S[1]\circ(\delta\otimes1_P)=d\circ e_J:Q\otimes_A^LP\longrightarrow S[1],$$
with the right-tensor shift comparison $(H_S[1])\otimes P=(H_S\otimes P)[1]$.

source.place: 08JC, section-hom-complexes and section-internal-hom; explicit evaluation calculation on the two cone summands

proof.text: Under the closed endpoint comparison, $e_S$ is evaluation on $Z$ followed by the support inclusion. To check the normalization, a local map $f:P\to i_*T$ corresponds under $i^*\dashv i_*$ to $\widetilde f:i^*P\to T$; its value on a local section $x$ is the image of $\widetilde f(i^*x)$ in $i_*T$. After applying $i^*$, this is exactly $\widetilde f(i^*x)$. The closed internal adjunction sends a map $i_*i^*P\to I$ to the same supported map, since its inverse is the support inclusion. Hence $i^*e_S$ is the evaluation-normalized derived tensor-Hom counit for $(C,E)$. Apply exact monoidal $i^*$ to Step 6, use $i^*S=E$, and substitute $u=\epsilon\delta$. The transpose of $i^*u$ is consequently $\epsilon\,b\circ i^*e_J$, with $b=i^*d$ as specified in the question.

source.place: 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), evaluation adjunction; 09XQ support inclusion and 0A45 support triangle

proof.text:
It remains to identify $e_J$ as the specified open cup/evaluation map. Under the slice adjunction in Step 4, a map into $J=j_*j^*I$ is its restriction into $j^*I$; thus the adjoint of $e_J:Q\otimes P\to J$ under $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ is the evaluation on $U$ after the two counits $j^*Q\to L^\vee$ and $j^*P\to L$. In a local free basis it sends $(f,x)$ to $f(x)$; these formulas commute with change of basis. By the definition of cup as the mate of the tensor of these counits, $e_J$ is exactly
$$Rj_*L^\vee\otimes_A^LRj_*L\xrightarrow{\mathrm{cup}}Rj_*(L^\vee\otimes_A^LL)\xrightarrow{Rj_*\mathrm{ev}}Rj_*A_U.$$
Apply $i^*$ and use Step 7 to obtain the asserted formula. All comparisons are adjunction maps or evaluation maps. Precomposition by a map $L\to M$ in the Hom factor and its action in the tensor factor satisfy $f(gx)=(f\circ g)(x)$; hence the identity is natural in $L$ in the usual contravariant/covariant pairing sense. The single sign comes from Step 4 and is independent of $L$.
